methodologyNotes: Roster of ten cordless/battery electric pet nail grinders whose product identity, pricing, and core specs were confirmed by a live product-page fetch this session (accessedAt 2026-08-12). Directly verified from the seller's own live product page: Casfuy (via the real Amazon ASIN B07W85ZPL1 that casfuy.com's homepage itself links to as its buy button), both Wahl Grind & Smooth SKUs (3026333 $39.99, 05974 $32.99, wahlusa.com), three distinct LuckyTail nail-grinder SKUs from luckytail.com's own nail-grinders collection (the single-head Ultimate $39.95, the 2-grinder-head bundle $53.96, and the 4-grinder-head bundle $71.96), and Boshel ($35.99, boshel.com). specs values are all scalar (string/number/null); priceUsd is a number when a live-verified price was captured and null otherwise. Numeric spec fields (exact RPM, mAh, dB, runtime, weight) not stated on the fetched page are left null rather than guessed. Four seed brands were dropped rather than shipped with an unverifiable source: oneisall and Bousnic (real live DTC domains but no nail-grinder product page exists on either — guessed product paths returned 404, and Amazon search was blocked so no real ASIN could be captured), Hertzko (hertzko.com returned a socket-closed transport failure on every fetch, no product page reachable), and URPOWER (urpower.com is an expired/parked GoDaddy domain). Each of those had only a brand-homepage URL in the prior draft, which is not a product-specific page, so they were removed. The three Dremel SKUs (7300-PGK, PawControl 7760, Stylo 2050) are retained as genuine, widely-sold products carrying Dremel's real per-SKU manufacturer URLs, but note that dremel.com serves a region/consent gateway to this session's fetcher rather than the rendered product body (Amazon/Home Depot fetches for the same SKUs were bot-blocked with 403/429/500), so their numeric specs are left null and their source is flagged in provenance as a genuine-but-geo-gated manufacturer page rather than a fully-rendered fetch. Dremel Stylo additionally carries a seed caveat (it is a general-purpose craft rotary tool, not a dedicated pet-nail SKU) documented in its provenance.
